nodes.name: Graphene synthesis
nodes.procedure: 4 mmol of glucose, 6 mmol of NH4Cl, and 80 g of KCl and NaCl with the weight ratio of 51:49 were first treated by ball-milling, and dried at 150°C for 8 h to form brown mixture. Then the mixture was pyrolyzed at 1050°C under N2 for 1 h with the heating rate of 35°C/min, followed by natural cooling to room temperature. Graphene forms after being ultrasonically rinsed with distilled water and ethanol several times.

nodes.name: PtIrCuNiCr HEA NPs on graphene via LSA
nodes.procedure: Various chloride salts were mixed in ethanol with 0.01 M for each metallic element. Taking the synthesis of PtIrCuNiCr as an example, the salt precursors of H2PtCl6·6H2O, H2IrCl6·6H2O, CuCl2·2H2O, NiCl2·6H2O, CrCl3·6H2O were first mixed in ethanol. The mixed solution was then directly dropped onto graphene with a loading of ~0.1 ml/mg, followed by ultrasonic treatment for ensuring the uniform salt load on graphene. The loaded substrates were transferred to a vacuum oven for drying at room temperature. For the synthesis of HEA nanoparticles (NPs) by the LSA method, the precursors-loaded graphene was firstly dispersed in hexane with 0.5 mg/ml by magnetic stirring. Hexane is used because the salt precursors are insoluble in it, ensuring the salts remain on substrates. Moreover, the oxygen-free structure of hexane is conducive in preventing the oxidation of the HEA NPs during LSA process. The solution was irradiated under agitation with the pulse laser for 30 min, ensuring all the substrates were irradiated by the laser beam.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show HEA NPs uniformly distributed on graphene with average diameter of 2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These HEA NPs are uniformly distributed on the graphene surface with an average radius of 2 nm (Figure 2B).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS maps display Pt, Ir, Cu, Ni, and Cr elements throughout the NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy maps display Pt, Ir, Cu, Ni, and Cr elements throughout these NPs (Figure 2C).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-scale HAADF-STEM shows homogeneous elemental distribution without segregation; disordered structures and stacking faults observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Homogeneous distribution of individual elements with no obvious segregation has been found even at the atomic scale (Figure 2D), manifesting the high-entropy character... HAADF-STEM images of PtIrCuNiCr NPs with obvious disordered structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS demonstrates HEA NPs loading on graphene is approximately 5 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy demonstrates that the actual HEA NPs loading on graphene is approximately 5 wt% (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms face-centered cubic phase; (111), (200), (220) peaks broadened, weakened, and shifted to higher angles vs Pt; strain 4-5x higher than pure Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern (Figure 2F) confirms the face-centered cubic phase of the HEA NPs... The strain in HEA NPs is four to five times that in pure Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows metallic bonding states of all five elements; characteristic peaks of Cu, Ni, and Cr show metallic and oxidized states; no Cl peaks detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The valence states of the HEA components are monitored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, Figure S3 and Table S2). The metallic bonding states of all five elements have been determined... The XPS peaks of Cl element were not detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis shows broad distributions of normal strains ε_xx, ε_yy perpendicular/in-plane to (200), and shear strain ε_xy across HEA NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the HEA NPs shown in Figure 3C, the strain ε_xx is perpendicular to the (200) plane, ε_yy is in the (200), and ε_xy is the sheer strain... Broad distributions of normal strain and shear strain have been found.
